datasets.title: LBNL simulated single-duct AHU (labelled faults)
datasets.summary: One simulated single-duct VAV air handler (cooling coil only, OA economizer) for a year at 1-minute resolution: a fault-free run plus stuck OA dampers, cooling-coil valve leaks and stuck valves, and OA / coil sensor biases at several severities.
teaches: outdoor-air fraction and a stuck outdoor-air damper
leaking cooling-coil valve
fault onset seen by drift detectors (spliced run)
scoring detectors against ground-truth labels
datasets.publisher: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (with PNNL, NREL, ORNL and Drexel University)
datasets.citation: Granderson, J., Lin, G., Chen, Y., Casillas, A., Im, P., Jung, S., Benne, K., Ling, J., Gorthala, R., Wen, J., Chen, Z., Huang, S., Vrabie, D. (2022). LBNL Fault Detection and Diagnostics Datasets. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. doi:10.25984/1881324
datasets.timezone: naive simulation clock (no DST); 1-minute samples, calendar year 2018
datasets.equipment: 1 single-duct AHU (cooling coil, economizer, 5 zone temperatures)

fault_types.damper: OA damper stuck at a fixed position
fault_types.valve_leak: cooling-coil valve leaks when commanded closed

default.description: fault-free + 4 stuck-damper runs + the single valve-leak run (the LBNL benchmark's SDAHU set) and a spliced fault-onset run

quirks.note: In every faulted run SA_SPSPT is a constant -400.25 (a placeholder, not a setpoint); masked to missing.

In the fault-free run SA_SP is not a measured static pressure: it holds ~402-403 (the ~1.61 inH2O setpoint in Pa) with the fan off as well as on; masked to missing. In the faulted runs SA_SP is the measured static in inH2O and is kept.
SA_CFM magnitudes (~3e5) are implausible for cfm and the units are undocumented; treat the airflow role as relative, not absolute.

known_issues: Supply static pressure is inconsistent across runs: the fault-free run exports the setpoint in Pa under SA_SP, the faulted runs a -400.25 placeholder under SA_SPSPT. Both are masked at ingest, so static-pressure rules decline where the data is bad.
Valve and damper signals are 0-1 fractions; they are rescaled to percent.
Valves and dampers map to the controller demand columns (*_DM), not the measured positions: a stuck device's position hides the fault the rules look for.
damper_stuck_100 is a short run (about 7 months).

The coi_leakage_010/025/040/050 members are byte-identical (same size and CRC), as are the four oa_bias_* members: they are one run each, not a severity sweep, so they cannot measure how detection varies with severity.

data_issues.title: SA_SPSPT is a -400.25 placeholder in every faulted run
data_issues.evidence: All 20 faulted runs export SA_SPSPT as the constant -400.25; the fault-free run exports the setpoint 1.60746 inH2O.

contradicts.document: SDAHU inventory Table 2 (SA_SPSPT: supply air duct static pressure setpoint, inches H2O)
contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

data_issues.handling_note: Masked to missing (mask quirk: values below -100), so static-pressure rules decline instead of reading a negative setpoint.

data_issues.title: Fault-free SA_SP is the static-pressure setpoint in Pa, not a measurement
data_issues.evidence: Fault-free SA_SP holds 401.9 with the fan off (median) and 403.5 with it on (range 401.8-410.6): ~1.61 inH2O expressed in Pa, and it never falls toward zero with the fan stopped. In the 20 faulted runs SA_SP is the measured static in inH2O (fan-on median 1.51-1.61, fan-off median 0.003-0.005).

contradicts.document: SDAHU inventory Table 2 (SA_SP: supply air duct static pressure, inches H2O)
contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

data_issues.handling_note: Masked to missing in the fault-free run (mask quirk: values above 100); the faulted runs' measured static is kept.

data_issues.title: SA_CFM and RA_CFM are not in cfm
data_issues.evidence: SA_CFM peaks at 1,266,232 and has a fan-on median of 596,187 -- implausible as cfm for one floor's air handler.

contradicts.document: SDAHU inventory Table 2 (SA_CFM / RA_CFM: supply / return airflow, CFM)
contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

data_issues.handling_note: Left as published; treat the airflow role as relative, not absolute.

datasets.title: LBNL simulated fan-powered VAV terminal units (labelled faults)
datasets.summary: Parallel (PFPU) and series (SFPU) fan-powered VAV boxes on one AHU for a year at 1-minute resolution: 31 runs each -- fault-free plus stuck VAV dampers, airflow and room-temperature sensor biases, reheat-valve leaks and sticks, reheat-coil fouling, unstable control and a restricted box fan. Faults are on the South-zone box.
teaches: zone-terminal airflow tracking and reheat
which box is the device under test (diff the faulted run against fault-free)
datasets.publisher: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (with PNNL, NREL, ORNL and Drexel University)
datasets.citation: Granderson, J., Lin, G., Chen, Y., Casillas, A., Im, P., Jung, S., Benne, K., Ling, J., Gorthala, R., Wen, J., Chen, Z., Huang, S., Vrabie, D. (2022). LBNL Fault Detection and Diagnostics Datasets. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. doi:10.25984/1881324
datasets.timezone: naive simulation clock (no DST); 1-minute samples, calendar year 2018
datasets.equipment: 4 fan-powered VAV boxes (_I/_W/_S/_E zones) per variant; the _S box is mapped

default.description: parallel-FPU fault-free + 2 stuck-damper + a stuck and a leaking reheat valve

known_issues: Faults are imposed on the SOUTH zone box (_S columns); the other zones stay healthy.
The reheat valve maps to the demand column (RH_VLV_DM_S); VAV_DMPR_S has no demand twin and is the measured position.
Scenario ids replace '%' with 'pct', '+' with 'p' and a leading '-' with 'm'.
No detector targets are declared yet: score reports overall detection only.

datasets.title: LBNL simulated chiller plant (labelled faults)
datasets.summary: A simulated water-side chiller plant (3 chillers, 3 cooling towers, primary and secondary loops) for a year at 1-minute resolution: fault-free plus cooling-tower fouling and PI mistuning, a condenser-bypass valve leaking or stuck, chiller fouling and sensor biases. No refrigerant-side points.
teaches: chiller kW/ton and cooling-tower approach
calibrating a design ceiling from the plant's own fault-free run
why a label swap in a published dataset must be fixed before analysis
datasets.publisher: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (with PNNL, NREL, ORNL and Drexel University)
datasets.citation: Granderson, J., Lin, G., Chen, Y., Casillas, A., Im, P., Jung, S., Benne, K., Ling, J., Gorthala, R., Wen, J., Chen, Z., Huang, S., Vrabie, D. (2022). LBNL Fault Detection and Diagnostics Datasets. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. doi:10.25984/1881324
datasets.timezone: naive simulation clock (no DST); 1-minute samples, calendar year 2018
datasets.equipment: 3 chillers, 3 cooling towers, primary/secondary CHW loops; unit 1 mapped

fault_types.bypass_valve: condenser-water bypass (three-way) valve leaking or stuck
fault_types.sensor_bias: chiller, tower or secondary-loop pressure sensor offset

default.description: fault-free + tower fouling + stuck bypass + a sensor bias

quirks.note: The exported outdoor dry-bulb (OA_TEMP) and wet-bulb (OA_TEMP_WB) columns are swapped relative to the dataset inventory; swapped back before mapping.
The secondary chilled-water loop's supply and return temperatures are swapped; swapped back before mapping (the primary loop is correct).

known_issues: Two label swaps in the export (outdoor wet/dry-bulb; secondary-loop supply/return) are fixed at ingest; see the quirks.
The simulated chiller/tower design curves are not published: calibrate the chiller_efficiency / cooling_tower_approach design ceilings from the fault-free run.
Water-side only: the refrigerant-side chiller drift detectors cannot run on it.

data_issues.title: Outdoor dry-bulb and wet-bulb columns are swapped
data_issues.evidence: The tower leaving-water setpoint follows max(wet-bulb + 8 F, 60 F): on the 210,661 minutes above the 60 F floor CT_SW_TEMPSPT equals OA_TEMP + 8 to a median 0.28 F but OA_TEMP_WB + 8 only to 6.27 F; OA_TEMP_WB exceeds OA_TEMP in 99.3% of rows (a wet-bulb cannot exceed its dry-bulb).

contradicts.document: Chiller-plant inventory Table 2 (OA_TEMP: dry bulb; OA_TEMP_WB: wet bulb) and Eq. 3 / Table 1 (tower setpoint = wet-bulb + 8 F)
contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

data_issues.handling_note: Swapped back before mapping (swap quirk), in every run.

data_issues.title: Secondary-loop supply and return temperatures are swapped
data_issues.evidence: In the 169,809 rows where the secondary loop carries load (CWL_SEC_LOAD > 10) the labelled return is colder than the labelled supply in 100% of rows, while the primary loop's return is warmer in 99.9% of them; hourly (supply - return) correlates +0.88 with CWL_SEC_LOAD.

contradicts.document: Chiller-plant inventory Table 2 (CWL_SEC_SW_TEMP: supply, CWL_SEC_RW_TEMP: return water temperature)
contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

data_issues.handling_note: Swapped back before mapping (swap quirk), in every run; the primary loop is left as published.

datasets.title: LBNL simulated boiler plant (labelled faults, Brick model)
datasets.summary: A simulated hot-water plant (2 boilers, 2 pumps, one loop) for a year at 1-minute resolution: fault-free plus boiler fouling, PI mistuning and boiler / loop temperature and pressure sensor biases, with the plant's Brick model.
teaches: hot-water loop differential-pressure reset
why a Brick On_Off_Status on a boiler is an enable, not proof of firing
a detection gap: boiler fouling is invisible to temperature-only rules
datasets.publisher: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (with PNNL, NREL, ORNL and Drexel University)
datasets.citation: Granderson, J., Lin, G., Chen, Y., Casillas, A., Im, P., Jung, S., Benne, K., Ling, J., Gorthala, R., Wen, J., Chen, Z., Huang, S., Vrabie, D. (2022). LBNL Fault Detection and Diagnostics Datasets. Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. doi:10.25984/1881324
datasets.timezone: naive simulation clock (no DST); 1-minute samples, calendar year 2018
datasets.equipment: 2 boilers, 2 hot-water pumps, 1 loop; boiler/pump 1 mapped

fault_types.sensor_bias: boiler / loop temperature or pressure sensor offset

default.description: fault-free + fouling + PI mistuning + a temperature sensor bias

quirks.note: BOI_STA_1/BOI_STA_2 are the boiler enable, not burner firing, so they are left unmapped; rules needing boiler_status decline on this plant.

known_issues: The boiler status points are enables (see the quirk); boiler_status is not mapped.
Gas use is a cumulative counter (BOI_GAS_CSUM_*) with no CAMBER role yet, so boiler fouling (a gas-per-heat signature) has no detector.

data_issues.title: BOI_STA is the boiler enable, not burner firing
data_issues.evidence: In the fault-free run BOI_STA_1 is 1 in 100% of rows while boiler 1 burns no gas (BOI_GAS_CSUM_1 = 0) in 50.5% of them.

contradicts.document: Boiler-plant inventory Table 2 (BOI_STA: on-off status of a boiler, 0-Off; 1-On)
contradicts.citation: LBNL FDD Data Sets, doi:10.25984/1881324; Granderson et al. 2023, Sci Data 10:342, doi:10.1038/s41597-023-02197-w

data_issues.handling_note: Left unmapped: mapping it to boiler_status would read every enabled-but-idle minute as firing, so rules needing boiler_status decline on this plant.

datasets.title: Building Data Genome 2 (whole-building meters)
datasets.summary: 3,053 hourly whole-building energy meters from 1,636 non-residential buildings on 19 sites, 2016-2017: electricity, chilled water, steam, hot water, gas, water, irrigation and solar, with site weather and building metadata.
teaches: change-point M&V baselines (ASHRAE Guideline 14 acceptance)
weather normalization with the site's own weather station
portfolio storage: one facility per site, one equipment per building meter
datasets.publisher: Building and Urban Data Science (BUDS) Lab, National University of Singapore
datasets.citation: Miller, C., Kathirgamanathan, A., Picchetti, B. et al. (2020). The Building Data Genome Project 2, energy meter data from the ASHRAE Great Energy Predictor III competition. Scientific Data 7, 368. doi:10.1038/s41597-020-00712-x

default.description: metadata + weather + cleaned electricity and chilled-water meters for up to 4 buildings on each of 10 sites (plus the buildings the M&V example uses)

full.description: all 19 files (raw, cleaned and the competition subset); ingest reads every site and every cleaned meter

known_issues: Licence is CC-BY-SA 4.0 (the repository LICENSE): analysis and commercial use are fine; a redistributed adaptation of the data must keep the same licence.
Meter readings are hourly energy per interval; they are stored as an hourly-mean rate (numerically equal), electricity under 'power' and the other meters under 'energy_rate'.
One facility per site (ds-bdg2-<site>); each building meter is an equipment '<building>__<meter>' of class '<METER>_METER'. Weather (airTemperature, degC) is converted to F on equipment 'weather'.
kaggle/kaggle.csv (the competition subset, numeric building ids) is downloaded by the full subset but not ingested; it is known to mix units across sites.
